responses.text: At the Planck scale—10^-35 meters—spacetime abandons every pretense of smoothness. Here, distance loses meaning, causality wavers, and before and after dissolve into probability. The stage on which all physics performs is, at bottom, not a stage at all—but a seething, restless storm of possibility.

Space and time themselves fragment into a turbulent, probabilistic churn, neither here nor there, existing and not existing simultaneously. Every notion of continuity shatters, replaced by a restless, bubbling geometry that defies imagination.

Virtual black holes wink into existence and evaporate before light could cross them; wormholes stitch and unstitch; the very notion of "here" dissolves into a probabilistic froth of overlapping shapes, each a different answer to the question of what shape means. There may be no points down there, no continuum, only a churning superposition of possible universes-in-miniature—and from that chaos, somehow, the serene flat vacuum we mistake for emptiness emerges.
